tour.welcomeContent: Here's a quick tour of your inbox. We'll highlight each part as we go — use the arrow keys to move between steps, or Esc to skip.
tour.triageContent: New emails land in this tab, most important first. Decide on each one: reply, archive, snooze — or prioritise it to move it to Action.
tour.backgroundSortingContent: We sorted your newest emails first so you could get started. The rest are still being processed in the background and will move into their categories as they're sorted. This bar shows how far along it is, and disappears when it's done.
tour.processContent: Prioritise an email to move it here. This is your focused workspace for emails that need action.
tour.actionContent: Emails you prioritise move to this tab. It's your focused to-do list for the emails that need real work.
tour.deliveryContent: Instead of trickling in all day, new emails arrive in batches. This bar shows when the next batch lands — urgent emails still come straight through.
tour.assistantContent: Each card shows who it's from, an AI summary and how urgent we think it is. Open one to get the AI side panel with tasks, notes and Ask AI. The next few steps show what its buttons do.
tour.priorityBadgeContent: Tap the priority badge on any email to see why we ranked it there: the score breakdown and the category we put it in. Think we got it wrong? Use Correct prioritization or change the category right there, and BearlyMail learns from it.
tour.prioritiseContent: Needs doing? Pick how urgent it is for you: Can wait, Get on it or Oh sh$t. Picking one moves the email to the Action tab, where your to-dos are sorted by priority.
tour.snoozeContent: Can't deal with it yet? Snooze hides the email and brings it back to your inbox when you choose. Click Snooze, type when you want it back, like 4h, 5pm, tomorrow or next Monday, and press Enter. In Gmail it syncs too.
tour.archiveContent: Done with it, or never needed it? Archive clears it from your list and archives it in Gmail or Outlook too. Nothing is deleted: you can still find it in All Mail. Shortcut: press Delete.
tour.blockContent: Never want to hear from someone again? Open this ⋮ menu and choose Block sender. Once you confirm, every future email from them is archived automatically. You can unblock them any time in Settings. (For newsletters, the menu offers Unsubscribe instead.)

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.description: How BearlyMail is different from a normal inbox, and the five-minute routine that makes it work.

section0.title: How BearlyMail works
section0.content: BearlyMail is built for people who find email overwhelming. Instead of one endless list, your email is split into three tabs, sorted by AI, and delivered in batches so it isn't interrupting you all day.
section0.item0: Triage: new emails, most important first. Decide what to do with each one.
section0.item1: Action: emails you've prioritised. This is your email to-do list.
section0.item2: Follow Up: threads where you're waiting on someone else to reply.

section1.title: Your first session
section1.item0: Connect your email account in Settings → Email Delivery → Email Accounts (Gmail, Outlook / Office 365, Zoho or any other IMAP account).
section1.item1: Give the AI some context in Settings → Guide Our AI, or click Analyze Emails to let it learn from your history.
section1.item2: Open Triage and work from the top. For each email: archive it, snooze it, or set a priority to move it to Action.
section1.item3: When Triage is clear, switch to Action and do the work.

section2.title: A simple daily routine
section2.content: Check BearlyMail when a new batch arrives, not all day. Clear Triage quickly (don't reply to anything that takes more than a couple of minutes, just prioritise it), then block out time to work through Action. Check Follow Up once a day to chase anything that's gone quiet.

section3.title: Want the guided tour again?
section3.content: Go to Help and click Replay walkthrough, or Settings → Account → Advanced → Troubleshooting → Replay tour.

triage.title: Triage tab
triage.description: Quickly decide what to do with each new email: archive, snooze or prioritise.

section0.title: What is the Triage tab?
section0.content: Triage is where new emails land. They're sorted by priority score, so the most important ones are at the top, and grouped into categories (like Newsletters or Clients) that you can expand and collapse.

section1.title: Four decisions per email
section1.item0: Prioritise it: pick Can wait, Get on it or Oh sh$t. The email moves to the Action tab.
section1.item1: Snooze it: hide it until a time you choose, then it comes back to your inbox.
section1.item2: Archive it: done with it, or never needed it. It's archived in Gmail or Outlook too, never deleted.
section1.item3: Block the sender: open the ⋮ menu on the email. Future emails from them are archived automatically.

section2.title: High priority first
section2.content: When you first open BearlyMail, Triage shows only emails rated High and above. The tab shows how many you're seeing out of the total, for example "Triage (3 of 499)". Once you've cleared the important ones you can choose to see the rest, or change the priority filter yourself with the filter button.

section3.title: Why it sometimes asks you to wait
section3.content: If you still have emails waiting in Action or Follow Up, BearlyMail adds a little friction before you dig into lower-priority new mail. You can say a short phrase out loud or tap 30 times to continue. It's there to stop new email from distracting you from the work you've already committed to.

section4.title: Working with categories
section4.item0: Archive All clears a whole category at once.
section4.item1: If you keep archiving a category without reading it, BearlyMail will offer to auto-archive it in future.
section4.item2: Think an email is in the wrong category? Tap its priority badge and use Edit next to the category.
section4.item3: Recategorise re-sorts your inbox if your categories have changed.

section5.title: Tips for fast triage
section5.item0: Use the keyboard: J/K to move, 1/2/3 to prioritise, E or Delete to archive (see Keyboard shortcuts).
section5.item1: Don't reply in Triage. If it needs more than two minutes, prioritise it and move on.
section5.item2: Cmd-click (Ctrl-click on Windows) emails to select several, or Shift-click to select a range, then snooze or archive them in one go.

action.title: Action tab
action.description: Your email to-do list: the emails you've prioritised, sorted by urgency.

section0.title: What is the Action tab?
section0.content: When you prioritise an email in Triage, it moves to Action. This is your focused to-do list for emails that need real work: a reply, a decision or a task. (This tab used to be called Process.)

section1.title: Priority levels
section1.content: Emails are sorted by the level you chose, then by priority score:
section1.item0: 🧨 Oh sh$t: drop everything.
section1.item1: 😀 Get on it: do it soon.
section1.item2: 😊 Can wait: needs doing, but not today.
section1.item3: Changed your mind? Pick a different level, or press 0 to clear the priority.

section2.title: Getting it done
section2.content: Open an email to see it alongside the AI side panel:
section2.item0: AI Summary: a TL;DR, bullet points, action items or what the sender is asking for.
section2.item1: Action Items: tasks pulled out of the email. Add your own, tick them off, or save them to Focus Bear.
section2.item2: Private Notes: notes on the thread that only you can see.
section2.item3: Ask AI: ask questions about the thread or get help drafting a reply.

section3.title: Replying
section3.content: Use Suggested Replies to get a starting draft. When you send, BearlyMail checks the tone of your email against your tone settings and flags anything that might land badly; you can use the suggested revision, disagree, or hold the button to send anyway. You can also schedule the email to send later.

section4.title: When is an email done?
section4.content: When you reply, choose when you expect to hear back. The thread leaves Action, and if they haven't replied by then it appears in Follow Up. If you still have work to do after replying, tick I still need to take action in the reply box to keep it in Action. Archive the email when you're completely finished.

followUp.title: Follow Up tab
followUp.description: Keep track of threads where you're waiting for a reply, and chase them with AI-drafted follow-ups.

section0.title: What is the Follow Up tab?
section0.content: Follow Up shows threads you're waiting on: you sent the last message and haven't heard back in the time you expected. It's your list of balls in other people's courts.

section1.title: Setting when you expect a reply
section1.content: When you reply or compose an email, choose Expect a reply within: 48 hours by default, or 3 days, 7 days, next Monday, 2 weeks or a custom time. BearlyMail keeps the thread out of your way until then, and if no reply has arrived it shows up in Follow Up. Choose No follow-up if you don't need a response.

section2.title: Chasing people up
section2.item0: Each thread shows how many days it's been since their last response and when the follow-up was due.
section2.item1: Generate Follow-ups writes a polite AI draft for every thread in view. Review and edit each one.
section2.item2: Send the drafts one at a time, or send them all together.
section2.item3: If open tracking is on, you'll see when the recipient opened your email.

section3.title: Clearing a thread
section3.content: When they reply, the thread leaves Follow Up and comes back to Action. If you no longer need a response, archive the thread.

priority.title: Priority scores and the priority badge
priority.description: Why an email is ranked where it is, and how to correct BearlyMail when it gets it wrong.

section0.title: The priority badge
section0.content: Every email shows a badge like "High Priority (42)". The label is the band and the number is the priority score. BearlyMail works the score out from the sender, the content, your context in Guide Our AI and how you've handled similar emails before.
section0.item0: Very High: 50 and above
section0.item1: High: 30 to 50
section0.item2: Medium: 15 to 30

section1.title: Tap the badge to see why
section1.content: Click or tap the badge to open the detail:
section1.item0: Score Breakdown: the factors that added to or took away from the score.
section1.item1: Who scored it: a rule you set up, a local model or the AI.
section1.item2: Category: which category the email was put in and why. Use Edit to move it to another one.
section1.item3: Correct prioritization: tell BearlyMail what score you expected and why.

section2.title: Teaching BearlyMail
section2.content: Every correction, category change and priority you set trains the AI, so rankings get better the more you use it. For lasting changes, add VIP contacts and describe what's urgent to you in Settings → Guide Our AI.

section3.title: Calculating and Not prioritised
section3.content: "Calculating..." means the score is still being worked out; it usually takes a few seconds. "Not prioritised" means scoring failed. Click the badge to try again.

section4.title: Urgent emails
section4.content: Truly urgent emails skip the batch and arrive straight away, marked "Urgent – delivered early". See Scheduled delivery.

delivery.title: Scheduled delivery
delivery.description: How email batching works, how to change delivery times, and when urgent emails break through.

section0.title: Why batch email?
section0.content: Every new email is an interruption. BearlyMail holds non-urgent email and delivers it in batches at times you choose, so you can focus in between. The bar at the top of your inbox shows when the next batch arrives.

section1.title: Changing your delivery times
section1.content: Go to Settings → Email Delivery → Email Batching and choose Calm (twice a day on weekdays), Balanced (four times a day on weekdays) or Always on (as soon as it arrives). To set your own, click Change, then pick the Delivery Days, add or remove Delivery Times and choose your timezone. Changes save by themselves.

section2.title: Urgent emails still get through
section2.content: BearlyMail regularly checks waiting emails for anything urgent. If an email is urgent enough, it's delivered right away, with an "Urgent – delivered early" label so you know why it arrived. The inbox bar shows when the last urgent check ran.

search.title: Search
search.description: Find any email by asking in plain English, or with search operators.

section0.title: Searching your email
section0.content: Open Search from the sidebar and type what you're looking for, like "emails from Sam about the budget" or "the invoice from last month". The AI turns your question into a search, runs it across your accounts and ranks the results by relevance.

section1.title: Search operators
section1.content: For precise searches you can use operators:
section1.item0: from:name or from:email@example.com
section1.item1: to:name
section1.item2: subject:words
section1.item3: has:attachment (Gmail)

section2.title: Searching more than one account
section2.content: Use Search in to choose which connected accounts to search. Gmail accounts support every Gmail operator. Other accounts support the most common ones (from:, to:, subject:, before: and after:) and search for anything else as plain text.

section3.title: Tips
section3.item0: Start with plain English; it's usually quicker than building a query.
section3.item1: Put exact phrases in quotes: "project proposal".

context.title: Guide Our AI
context.description: Tell BearlyMail about you and your work so it ranks your email the way you would.

section0.title: Why context matters
section0.content: BearlyMail's AI decides what's important using what it knows about you. The more accurate your context, the better your Triage order. Find it in Settings → Guide Our AI → Context About Me.

section1.title: What you can tell it
section1.item0: VIP Contacts: people whose emails should always rank highly.
section1.item1: Info About Me: your role and responsibilities.
section1.item2: Current Projects & Topics: what you're focused on right now.
section1.item3: What I Consider Urgent: the situations that should break through batching.
section1.item4: What I Don't Consider Important: things to rank lower, like certain notifications.
section1.item5: Q&A: common questions and your answers, which the auto-responder can use.

section2.title: Let BearlyMail learn for you
section2.content: Click Analyze Emails to have the AI read your email history and suggest context, VIP contacts and categories. Review its suggestions and keep the ones that are right.

section3.title: Categories and rules
section3.content: In the same tab you can edit your email categories, group them into families, and set up category rules (for example, everything from a domain goes to Clients). Learned priority rules shows what BearlyMail has picked up from your corrections.

section4.title: Tips
section4.item0: Be specific: "emails about the Q3 launch" beats "work emails".
section4.item1: Update your projects when your priorities change.
section4.item2: Correct rankings from the priority badge; it's the fastest way to teach the AI.
